components.css: .ds-module { overflow: hidden; color: var(--ink, #eef3ff); border: 1px solid var(--line, #5b6882); border-radius: 10px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--panel-2, rgba(29,33,44,.97)), var(--panel, rgba(19,22,30,.97))); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.05), 0 5px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.18); font: 11px/1.42 Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-module__title { position: relative; margin: 0; padding: 5px 28px 5px 20px; color: #eef2fb; border-bottom: 1px solid #54617b; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #30384a 0%, #1a1f2b 54%, #121722 55%, #2a3142 100%); font: 800 10px/1.25 Tahoma, Verdana, sans-serif; letter-spacing: .18px; text-transform: lowercase; } .ds-module__title::before { content: '✦'; position: absolute; left: 7px; top: 5px; color: #79b6ff; font-size: 9px; } .ds-module__title::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 7px; right: 8px; width: 18px; height: 5px; border: 1px solid rgba(142,159,194,.45); background: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(117,151,255,.7) 0 45%, transparent 45% 60%, rgba(184,255,44,.68) 60%); } .ds-module__body { padding: 8px; } .ds-module:focus-within { border-color: var(--line-bright, #8495b7); }

components.css: .ds-nav { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 5px; } .ds-nav a { display: block; padding: 5px 8px; color: #eef2fb; border: 1px solid #586684; border-radius: 7px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #33405b 0%, #20273a 46%, #27365f 48%, #1c2230 100%); font: 700 9px/1.42 Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, sans-serif; text-align: center; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav a:hover { color: #fff; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #4d76ff, #1a45ce); } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--lime, #b8ff2c); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #060806; } .ds-nav a:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.css: .ds-work-row { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(120px,auto); gap: 8px; align-items: baseline; padding: 6px 7px 6px 17px; color: #f0f4ff; border-bottom: 1px solid #364054; font: 11px/1.42 Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, sans-serif; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; } .ds-work-row::before { content: '★'; position: absolute; left: 4px; top: 7px; color: #8aaeff; font-size: 8px; } .ds-work-row__title { font-weight: 700; } .ds-work-row__meta { color: #aebbd2; font-size: 8px; text-align: right; } .ds-work-row:hover { color: #fff; background: #2558ff; text-decoration: none; } .ds-work-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--lime, #b8ff2c); outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #060806; } .ds-work-row:active { transform: translateX(1px); }

components.css: .ds-github-stats { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 1px; margin: 0; border: 1px solid #364054; background: #364054; font-family: Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-github-stats div { min-width: 0; padding: 5px; background: #111620; } .ds-github-stats dt { color: #8fa0ba; font-size: 7px; } .ds-github-stats dd { margin: 1px 0 0; color: var(--ink, #eef3ff); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-github-stats div:hover { background: #182035; } .ds-github-stats div:focus-within { outline: 2px solid var(--lime, #b8ff2c); outline-offset: -2px; }

components.css: .ds-player { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 52px minmax(0,1fr); gap: 8px; align-items: center; color: #bec8dc; font: 8px/1.42 Tahoma, Verdana, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-player__disc { display: block; width: 52px; height: 52px; border: 1px solid #707fa0; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at center, #0b0d12 0 5px, #dff7ff 6px 8px, #315cff 9px 11px, #e8edf6 12px 17px, #8793a8 18px 20px, #161922 21px 25px); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #10131a, 0 0 10px rgba(48,97,255,.14); animation: ds-spin 10s linear infinite; } .ds-player__copy { display: grid; gap: 2px; min-width: 0; } .ds-player__copy a { overflow: hidden; color: #f2f5fc; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-player__copy a:hover { color: #fff; background: #2558ff; } .ds-player__copy a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--lime, #b8ff2c); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-player__bar { display: block; height: 4px; margin-top: 4px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid #55617b; border-radius: 5px; background: #1d2230; } .ds-player__bar span { display: block; width: 62%; height: 100%; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--violet, #aa87ff), #315cff, var(--cyan, #74e9ff), var(--lime, #b8ff2c)); } @keyframes ds-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-player__disc { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
postigo.sh is a compact, authored corner of the web that makes professional evidence immediately legible. It borrows the density, directness, and material tactility of a cared-for personal homepage: dark blue desktop space, steel-framed modules, metallic titlebars, terse labels, tiny live-status surfaces, and a resident goat that makes the system unmistakably Piero's.

The world is preview-native, pinned from direction seed e23380ff. It rejects the generic portfolio hero-and-card stack without becoming a Windows clone: this is a normal, route-first site whose modules look like a personal desktop. The homepage is the densest expression; stable Work, About, Resume, Writings, Contact, and project-case routes use the same material and type system with more reading room. Project-window interaction is intentionally outside this system until that behavior is implemented and documented separately.

unreviewed and undocumented is unfinished; this build ends with the finish review, the verdict, and DESIGN.md
keyCharacteristics: Compact Tahoma-led information density with Courier New reserved for system metadata.
Midnight blue-black surfaces, cool steel borders, and metallic gradient titlebars.
Blue, cyan, violet, and acid-lime signals used as state and wayfinding accents.
Hard-edged controls inside softly clipped modules; no modern pill-card language.
The embedded goat is a recurring signature, not a separate branding campaign.
Stable routes and honest public-presence states outrank decorative exploration.

rules.name: The Signal, Not Wash Rule
rules.body: Cyan, violet, and lime identify states or authored moments; they do not become full-screen decorative washes.

rules.name: The Honest State Rule
rules.body: Unavailable public data stays muted and explicit. Never recolor an unavailable state to resemble success or activity.

rules.name: The Tahoma First Rule
rules.body: New interface modules inherit Tahoma; do not introduce a display font to manufacture personality.

rules.name: The Mono Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Courier New is for metadata, timestamps, labels, and archival mechanics—not paragraphs or primary navigation.

rules.name: The First-Viewport Rule
rules.body: At desktop width, visitors must be able to identify Piero, see selected work, and locate public presence without opening or dragging anything.

rules.name: The Main Column Leads Rule
rules.body: Side rails provide context; the engineering identity, Work path, and evidence remain visually dominant.

rules.name: The Border Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: A component must read through its hard border and tonal surface before shadow is added.

rules.name: The No Fake Chrome Rule
rules.body: Metallic titlebars label modules; they never display inert window controls.

rules.name: The Radius Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Large containers may be softly clipped, but actions and data rows stay hard and compact. Avoid pill-shaped navigation and rounded SaaS cards.

dos: Do lead the first desktop viewport with identity, selected work, stable routes, and honest presence.
Do use one-pixel borders, metallic gradients, and restrained inset highlights to make depth tactile.
Do keep the goat embedded as a small resident signature in authored moments.
Do keep interactions semantic, keyboard-visible, route-first, and reduced-motion safe.
Do adapt content order and density at 780px; mobile is one direct column.
Do preserve the preview-native direction selected from seed e23380ff.
donts: Don't regress to a generic centered hero followed by interchangeable portfolio cards.
Don't turn the system into literal Windows cosplay, terminal cosplay, glassmorphism, neon cyberpunk, or rounded SaaS chrome.
Don't add fake minimize, maximize, close, drag, or resize affordances to ordinary site modules.
Don't invent posts, photos, activity, metrics, or professional claims to fill empty surfaces.
Don't let cyan, violet, or lime become decorative full-screen washes.
Don't treat project-window behavior as implemented visual-system law; it is explicitly deferred.
